To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have established an effective and efficient strategy for the evaluation of transporter-mediated drug interactions in the pharmaceutical industry.

(i) the use of in vivo animal PK and tissue distribution data, together with in vitro transporter data, is an important tool for predicting the risk of transporter-based drug interactions in the pharmaceutical industry and (ii) systems approaches, such as PBPK and mathematical modeling, are important tools for the prediction of drug distribution in the target tissues and the prediction of the risk of transporter-related adverse effects.

the in vitrosystems for transporter evaluation are useful for predicting transporter-mediated drug-drugs interactions and that the in vivo data are important for understanding the mechanisms of transporter-mediated drug distribution and elimination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies and approaches for the evaluation of new chemical entity as hepatic transporter substrate.
the application of hepatic transporter studies in the pharmaceutical industry to meet the regulatory requirements and future steps to improve the prediction accuracy of drug interactions.
the evaluation of hepatic transport systems in drug discovery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evaluation of hepatic transporter interactions is a key factor for successful drug development.
the application of the systems approach in the evaluation of drug transporters in the discovery stage has improved the efficiency of drug discovery and development.

the evaluation of new chemical entity as a transporter substrate has improved to meet regulatory requirements, and future steps should be to identify the risk of drug-drug interactions in humans at an early stage in drug development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the application of hepatic transport studies to the pharmaceutical industry has become more and more important to meet the requirements for regulatory submission and to identify promising compounds in drug discovery.
the application of the systems approach to the evaluation of drug transporters has been useful for the development of new medicines.
transporter studies are important for the prediction of pharmacological and toxic effects in the early stage of drug discovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evaluation of drug-drug interactions in humans is not always required, and that the in vitri data obtained in the preclinical stage are sufficient in many cases to predict drug-drug interactions.
the application of hepatic transporter research in the pharmaceutical industry is evolving in response to the regulatory guidelines for drug interactions.
the in vit ro data obtained for regulatory submissions are not always consistent with the in vivo data obtained during drug development.
